FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft finalized by the WaterProofing and Damp-Proofing Sectional Committee had been approved by Civil Engineering Divisiop Council. Glass fibre base coal tar pitch outerwraps are extensively used for corrosion protection of buried mild steel pipelines. These are generally used for protecting the inner wraps from damage or in wet conditions. In the formulation of this standard due weightage has been given to international co-ordination among the standards and practices prevailing in different countries in addition to relating it to the practices in the field in this country. The composition of the technical committee responsible for the formulation of this standard is given at Annex B. is complied with, the final value, rounded off in accordance with of significant places retained in standard.

3.3 Mineral Filler It shall consist of finely divided suitable inert mineral matter which is insoluble in water and passes through 75 microns IS Sieve [see IS 460(Part l)]. 3.4 Mineral Powder for Surfacing 3.4.1 Mineral powder matter such as talc or microns IS Sieve [see IS through 250 microns IS may also be used, 3.4.2 Weight material shall be as shall be powdered mineral mica passing through 600 460 (Part 1)]. 4 MANUFACTURE Outerwraps are made from glass fibre mat coated with plasticized coal tar enamel and dusted with mineral powder to prevent the layers from sticking together when rolled. The finished outerwrap shall have a smooth uniform surface free from visible defects.

Test samples shall not be taken from damaged portion of the roll, if any. METHODS OF TEST FOR TESTING VARIOUS PROPERTIES OF GLASS FIBRE TISSUE

A-1 METHODS OF TEST FOR TESTING WEIGHT OF GLASS FIBRE TISSUE A-1.1 Test Piece Cut out approximately about 2 m from the roll. Measure and cut a sample exactly 100 cm x 100 cm A-1.2 Procedure Weigh the sample in a balance having an accuracy of 0.5 g and record the results. NOTE-- For easier weighing, the piece of 100 cm x 100 cm
may be cut in smal Ier sizes and weighed together.

A-2 METHOD OF TEST FOR MINATION OF TISSUE THICKNESS A-2.1 Principles

DETER-

The thickness of glass fibre tissue is determined by placing sample on a glass plate, and a metallic cylinder of foot and anvil area both 6.45 cmz exerting a pressure 3

A-2.3.3 Press the clamp to lift the metallic cylinder to allow for insertion of the sample and gently lower the cylinder to rest on the sample. A-2.3.4 Measure the thickness at 12 equally spaced

IS 14695:1999 areas through a dial gauge having a least count of 0.01 mm. The loading given shall be 35 g/cm2. A-2.3.5 The average of 12 readings are taken as the mean thickness and recorded to the accuracy of 0.01 mm. A-2.4 Calculation A-3.3.2 Apply load along the length of the sample"by moving the lower jaws of the testing machine away from the upper jaws at about 250 mmhninutes. A-3.3.3 Note the breaking load as P,.

A-3.3 Procedure A-3.3.1 For each of the samples cut two lengths of adhesive tape measuring approximately 30 cm x 5 cm. Take sample No. 1, wrap and stick each length of adhesive tape over the 10 cm wide ends. This is a precaution taken for the testing of' a membrane material like RP tissue. The tape enables better gripping of the sample in the tensile machine gripping jaws.

The apparatus shall consist essentially of a suction fan for drawing air through a known area of _glass tibre tissue, a circular orifice over which the tissue to be tested can be clamped. A means of measuring the pressure drop across the mat, and means of measuing the volume of air flowing through the tissue.
